samples.summary: No test that PATCH /documents/:id now drops unknown body fields (mass-assignment regression would be invisible)
samples.evidence: The diff replaces `data: body` (the whole request body spread straight into `prisma.document.update`) with an explicit whitelist building `Prisma.DocumentUpdateInput` from `title` and `folderId` only (documents.controller.ts, `update`). The handler takes an inline `@Body() body: { title?; folderId? }`, not a DTO class, so the global `ValidationPipe({whitelist:true})` in main.ts:66 cannot strip anything — the controller whitelist is the only protection. Every new `update` test in documents.controller.spec.ts passes only `title` and/or `folderId` (lines 177-254); none sends an extra field such as `authorID`, `workspaceId`, `type` or `fileId` and asserts it is absent from the `updateDocument` argument. A future edit reverting to a spread, or adding a field to the loop, would keep the whole suite green while letting an API-key caller rewrite document ownership/workspace.
searchedFor: checked packages/backend/src/document/document.dto.spec.ts pattern for a documents PATCH DTO spec

samples.summary: Nothing asserts CombinedAuthGuard/WorkspaceScopeGuard are mounted on the new folders controller, and its list/create handlers do no workspace check of their own
samples.evidence: `ApiV1FoldersController.list` (folders.controller.ts:107-110) and `create` (88-105) trust the route `workspaceId` outright — the only thing refusing an API key minted for another workspace is the class-level `@UseGuards(CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard, ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard)`. folders.controller.spec.ts instantiates the controller with `new ApiV1FoldersController(...)`, so guards never run there, and the only guard-mounting test added (api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts:64-78) asserts solely that `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` is in `__guards__` — it does not check `WorkspaceScopeGuard`. So dropping or reordering that guard would leak/allow writes to another workspace's folder tree with the whole suite green. No e2e covers the new surface either (packages/backend/test/folder.e2e-spec.ts exercises only the web `folders/:id` routes; grep for 'api/v1' in it finds nothing).

samples.summary: folders `create` only asserts the cross-workspace parent check was called, never that a failing check blocks the create
samples.evidence: The test 'checks a supplied parent belongs to the route workspace' (folders.controller.spec.ts:62-65) leaves `assertSameWorkspace` mocked to resolve and asserts only `toHaveBeenCalledWith('f-9', WS)`. There is no companion test where `assertSameWorkspace` rejects and `folderService.create` is asserted not to have been called — unlike the equivalent documents test ('refuses a folder from another workspace', documents.controller.spec.ts:216). If the `await` were dropped or the call moved after `create`, the mock-call assertion would still pass and a folder could be created under a parent in another workspace.

samples.summary: The new HttpClient folder/copy/move methods are mocked away; no test exercises their real verb, path or body
samples.evidence: folders.test.ts:22-32 replaces the entire `HttpClient` class (`vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js')`), so `listFolders`, `createFolder`, `renameFolder`, `moveFolder`, `deleteFolder`, `copyDocument` and `moveDocument` in packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:311-344 are never executed. The `--dry-run` assertions do check URLs, but the preview strings are hand-built inside the commands (e.g. commands/folders.ts:69 `PATCH /folders/${seg(folderId)}`), duplicating the client's path rather than deriving it — so a wrong verb or path in the client (or a `createFolder` body that drops `parentId`) passes both the dry-run tests and the mocked-call tests. The existing real-fetch suites (test/http-client-paths.test.ts, test/http-client.test.ts) were not extended to cover the new methods.

samples.summary: 'Move to root' via explicit null parentId/folderId is only covered by unit tests that bypass the ValidationPipe and DTO
samples.evidence: The CLI deliberately sends `{parentId: null}` / `{folderId: null}` (commands/folders.ts move, commands/docs.ts move) and the controllers branch on `!== undefined` (folders.controller.ts:123, documents.controller.ts update). Whether an explicit `null` survives `UpdateFolderDto`'s `@IsOptional() @IsUUID()` under the global `ValidationPipe({whitelist:true})` is asserted nowhere: there is no packages/backend/src/folder/folder.dto.spec.ts (the repo has that pattern for document/workspace/bigquery DTOs), and the new /api/v1 routes have no e2e. If the pipe rejected or stripped the null, the whole 'return to root' feature 400s or silently no-ops while every unit test stays green. (The equivalent web route has the same shape, so this may already work in practice — hence medium confidence.)

samples.summary: The 'both halves land together' assertion on removeMember verifies nothing about the transaction
samples.evidence: createMockPrisma's `$transaction` mock invokes the callback with the same top-level prisma mock (workspace.service.spec.ts:41-43), so `expect(prisma.apiKey.updateMany).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` holds identically whether or not the write happens inside the transaction callback, and `expect(prisma.$transaction).toHaveBeenCalled()` (line 338, commented 'Both halves land together, so a key cannot survive a committed removal') only records that some transaction was opened. The atomicity the comment claims is untested; the comment overstates the coverage. Contained — the `updateMany` where/data assertions above it are real coverage of the revocation itself.

samples.summary: Small folders `update` gaps: no combined name+parent call, no empty-body call, and rename never asserts the manager check is skipped
samples.evidence: documents.controller.spec.ts has 'renames and moves in one call' (line 245) but folders.controller.spec.ts has no equivalent, so nothing checks `data` carries both `name` and `parentId` (folders.controller.ts:121-137). Likewise no test for an empty body (which reaches `folderService.update(id, {})`), and 'lets any member rename a folder they do not own' asserts only the `update` args, never `expect(workspaceService.assertMember).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` — so a rename accidentally gaining the manager gate would not be caught.

samples.summary: folders registration in the shipped cli.ts program is unasserted
samples.evidence: namespaces.test.ts builds its own program and calls `registerFoldersCommand` explicitly (lines 12-22), so it cannot catch a missing registration in src/cli.ts. The one test that inspects the real `buildProgram()` from '../src/cli.js' — output.test.ts:921 'wires every namespace onto the default program' — uses an `arrayContaining` list (login…schema) that does not include 'folders'. A dropped `registerFoldersCommand(program)` in cli.ts would leave the suite green; it would fail loudly on first use, hence nit.

verdict.reason: The finding's blocking premise — that a revert to spreading the body into prisma.document.update "would keep the whole suite green" — is false. The update tests assert the exact Prisma `data` object with Jest's plain-object `toHaveBeenCalledWith` (recursive exact equality), so the mapped shape is pinned: documents.controller.spec.ts:195-198 expects `data: {folder:{connect:{id:'f-1'}}}` for body `{folderId:'f-1'}`, :210-213 expects `data: {folder:{disconnect:true}}` for `{folderId:null}`, and :250-253 expects `data: {title:'New', folder:{connect:{id:'f-1'}}}`. Under `data: body` all three fail immediately, so the named mass-assignment regression cannot ship undetected; the whitelist behavior of documents.controller.ts:122-149 is already guarded. It is true that no test sends an extra field such as authorID/workspaceId (I read documents.controller.spec.ts in full, plus api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts:228-234, folder.e2e-spec.ts:287-295, authenticated-http.e2e-spec.ts:163-174, folders.controller.spec.ts:117-181), but the residual uncovered case is only a hypothetical future edit that explicitly copies a new field into `data` — a contained edge case (minor) while the changed core behavior is exactly asserted, not a major unguarded change under this lens.

finding.evidence: `ApiV1FoldersController.list` (folders.controller.ts:107-110) and `create` (88-105) trust the route `workspaceId` outright — the only thing refusing an API key minted for another workspace is the class-level `@UseGuards(CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard, ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard)`. folders.controller.spec.ts instantiates the controller with `new ApiV1FoldersController(...)`, so guards never run there, and the only guard-mounting test added (api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts:64-78) asserts solely that `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` is in `__guards__` — it does not check `WorkspaceScopeGuard`. So dropping or reordering that guard would leak/allow writes to another workspace's folder tree with the whole suite green. No e2e covers the new surface either (packages/backend/test/folder.e2e-spec.ts exercises only the web `folders/:id` routes; grep for 'api/v1' in it finds nothing).

verdict.reason: Verified directly. ApiV1FoldersController relies entirely on the class-level @UseGuards(CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard, ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard) (folders.controller.ts:38-39) for workspace isolation — list/create take the route workspaceId at face value, and update/remove only compare folder.workspaceId to the route param, never the caller's workspace. The unit spec builds the controller with `new ApiV1FoldersController(...)` (folders.controller.spec.ts:38-41), so no guard ever executes; all 20+ tests stay green with the guards deleted. The single mounting assertion in the repo (api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts:64-78) checks only `toContain(ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard)`. I searched wide for a counterexample: `__guards__` occurs exactly once repo-wide; `WorkspaceScopeGuard` appears in only its own spec and docs-content.controller.spec.ts:87 where `.overrideGuard()` is used (which silently no-ops if the guard is absent, so it asserts nothing about mounting); api-v1.module.ts:35-73 registers no APP_GUARD; and no e2e exercises /api/v1/workspaces/:id/folders (api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts covers only /documents, folder.e2e-spec.ts only the web routes, and `folders` appears nowhere else under packages/backend/test). Removing or reordering WorkspaceScopeGuard on this controller would let an API key minted for one workspace read and mutate another workspace's folder tree with the whole suite passing — a silently weakened guard on a new user-reachable write surface, which the rubric grades major.
